payload.stem: A team wants to test how long-term mild stress affects the immune systems of mice. Which proposal best follows ethical guidelines for research with animals?

options.text: Keep the stress as mild as the question allows and provide humane care, and begin right away because mild stress does not need committee review.
options.why: Even mild procedures with animals require institutional review before the study begins.

options.text: Have a committee review the plan and provide humane care, but raise the stress to the level that produces the largest change in the immune system.
options.why: Stress should be limited to what the research question requires, and maximizing the size of the effect is not a justification for greater distress.

options.text: Have a committee review the plan and keep the stress mild, but house the mice alone in bare cages to keep the conditions as simple as possible.
options.why: Humane housing and care are required, and barren isolation can add distress and also confound the results.

options.text: Have a committee review the plan, keep the stress as mild and brief as the question allows, and provide humane care.
options.why: Ethical animal research requires review, minimizing harm consistent with the research question, and humane care throughout the study.
